summary: This benchmark investigates causal representation transplantation from a 7B donor (Qwen2.5-Coder-7B) into a 72B recipient (Qwen2.5-72B) across variable-binding and overwrite tasks in Python execution contexts. Using a registered 7-dimensional affine interface, the authors demonstrate that a low-dimensional intervention at the relevant assignment token switches the recipient's output in 193 of 206 test groups (matching full-state exchange performance of 192/206), while exposing subtle interference from later overwrites. The study is methodologically rigorous, thoroughly controlled, and candid about failing its registered 95% preservation floor (achieving 94.66%).
strengths: Rigorous experimental design incorporating both positive controls (full-state exchange) and negative controls (equal-norm orthogonal edits).
Preregistered design and transparent reporting of results, including candidly acknowledging when the preservation rate (94.66%) fell one group short of the registered 95% threshold.
Careful error taxonomy showing that all 14 individual preservation failures specifically reflected intrusions from the subsequent variable overwrite rather than random corruption.
Comprehensive environmental documentation including hardware configuration (Apple M5 Ultra), memory allocation (147.24 GB), and package version pinning.
weaknesses: The evaluation does not test a full-state exchange control at the overwrite site, leaving open whether the 14 intrusion failures are specific to the low-dimensional transplant or a broader property of the recipient model's architecture.

The study is limited to a synthetic variable-binding and integer-arithmetic task on a single model pair (Qwen2.5-Coder-7B into Qwen2.5-72B), limiting direct generalizability to complex programmatic reasoning.
The submission lacks a formal repository attachment in metadata, relying instead on commit-pinned inline URLs.
suggestions: Perform the full-state exchange intervention at the overwrite token position to determine if the recipient's vulnerability to later-value intrusion is an inherent model dynamic or an artifact of the 7D affine projection.
Evaluate whether varying the number of intervening distractor assignments alters the intrusion rate during irrelevant-site edits.
Formally link the GitHub repository in the metadata section rather than relying solely on inline markdown links.

claims.text: A seven-dimensional transplant into frozen Qwen2.5-72B switched all four correct answers in 193 of 206 paired groups involving a saved Python value and a later overwrite.
A full-state exchange at the relevant assignment switched 192, and an equal-norm orthogonal edit switched zero.
Editing the irrelevant assignment preserved 195 of 206 groups (94.66%), one group short of the registered 95% floor.
Interchange intervention and causal abstraction frameworks provide established foundations for neural network representation swapping.

novelty_vs_existing.title: Causal abstractions of neural networks
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Extends interchange interventions from within-model causal abstraction to cross-model activation transplantation across disparate scales (7B to 72B) via low-dimensional affine maps in sequential code execution tasks.
